commits.message:
fix(pretty): indent guides draw a │ at each level (rich-pretty-v7b) (#257)

* fix(pretty): indent guides draw a │ at each level (rich-pretty-v7b)

The guide was a space styled with a foreground colour, which draws nothing.
It is now Rich's with_indent_guides: a │ (| when ASCII-only) in the first
cell of each whole indent, styled repr.indent, swapped in cell for cell so
the highlighter's spans stay put.

Console.print formats data with guides off, as Rich's print does. Tying
guides to highlight only went unnoticed while they were invisible.

* fix(pretty): guides stand in the structure's margin, off by default (rich-pretty-v7b)

The formatter records each line's margin where it starts the line, and
guides are drawn there rather than read back out of the whitespace, so a
wrapped string or a toString's own indent gets no guide inside it. Off by
default and never on an ASCII-only console, as in Rich; blank rows carry
the guide; indent: 0 no longer throws.

Addresses /code-review high on PR #257.

* fix(pretty): every margin is written, so a guide never takes a continued line's text (rich-pretty-v7b)

A row that looks empty can still be continued by a separator, a Map's
arrow or a key's value; its margin is now spaces like any other, and the
ASCII-only choice goes through drawable.

Addresses /code-review medium on PR #257.

* fix(pretty): a hanging row's guides are its slot's; margins always written (rich-pretty-v7b)

Frame carries the slot's margin, so a value after a wrapped key gets its
slot's guides and a hanging row can no longer start left of it (the
negative repeat). Every margin is written and a line with nothing past it
is cleared in the one final pass, so blank rows keep no trailing spaces.
An ASCII-only console gets no guide spans at all; the trailing-space trim
scans back instead of backtracking.

Not taken: copying margins per level (toText at 1000 levels 520ms vs
master's 435ms; the render around it is ~40s either way).

Addresses the step-12 /code-review high on PR #257.

* test(pretty): the thousand-level render runs at default options again (rich-pretty-v7b)

With guides on, each line is a thousand words for the render to wrap, which
timed out in CI (191s vs master's ~5s); guides are off by default now, and
the test's claim is about the default.
